guidance.heading: UPDATED 2026 FULL YEAR GUIDANCE
section: The Company’s outlook includes Adjusted EBITDA and Net Leverage, which are non-GAAP
measures. The Company does not provide certain estimated future results for Adjusted EBITDA and
Net Leverage on a GAAP basis because the Company is unable to predict, with reasonable certainty,
certain items that are excluded from Adjusted EBITDA, including but not limited to stock-based
compensation, strategic transaction costs, refinancing and debt-related costs, foreign exchange gain/
loss on intercompany loans, plus interest, taxes, and depreciation and amortization. These items are
uncertain and will depend on several factors, including industry conditions, and could be material to
the Company’s results computed in accordance with GAAP. The Company has not provided

desk.headline: Revenue up 5% to $461m, in line; adjusted EPS $0.38 beat; 2026 EBITDA growth guidance raised to ~10%
results: Revenue rose 5% to $461m, with volume/mix and price each adding about half; North America grew 8% while International slipped 1%, mainly on currency.
Gross margin widened about 240 bps to 39.4%, helped by volume, pricing and a one-off tariff refund that offset steel and freight inflation.
Adjusted EBITDA rose 14% to $127m (27.5% margin); North America's segment margin rose to 32.4% from 28.9%.
Net income doubled to $65m as interest costs fell by about $20m after last year's debt reduction.
The company repaid $45m of debt and bought back $75m of shares; net leverage fell to 2.25x.

guidance.summary: Alliance raised its 2026 adjusted EBITDA growth outlook to about 10%, the top of its earlier 8–10% range, and kept revenue growth at 6–7%. It now sees net leverage of about 2.1x at year-end (earlier 2.0x, set before the $75m buyback), interest of about $75m and about 203m diluted shares.

points: The tariff refund added about $5m in the quarter; all refunds applied for have now been received, so no more are expected.
Management said demand for laundromat (vended) equipment is strong and the slowdown is about permitting and construction delays, not weaker demand.
Steel costs, including some spot-price buying, are expected to squeeze fourth-quarter profitability.
Price increases for early 2027 have been announced to customers.
Paying down debt stays the top priority; the $75m buyback was tied to a share sale by the main shareholder, and further buybacks have no set timing.
